newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly up on exports, wheat.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly up on exports, wheat.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended mostly higher on Thursday, boosted by USDA's weekly export figure which was above trade expectations and on near-limit gains in wheat, traders said.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soymeal during the week ended April 10 totaled 139,400 tonnes, above expectations for 40,000 to 60,000 tonnes.
But soyoil net export sales totaled 1,400 tonnes, below expectations for 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes.
Traders said they had expected exports to taper off as Brazil continued to ship record quantities.
Soy products also drew strength from near-limit gains in wheat tied to news the European Union ended the bulk of its July/June wheat export sales on Thursday by closing its weekly tender system.

"We tried to go lower the last two days and didn't make it stick," said Dave Armstrong, analyst with ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp. "Good soybean meal sales were supportive, but all of that had us only a little higher until wheat took off."
Soymeal closed $2.90 per ton higher to $0.60 lower with May up $2.90 at $276.20. Soyoil ended 0.07 to 0.02 cent per lb higher with May up 0.05 at 24.09 cents.
Soy products also drew support from belief that Wednesday's losses, tied to reports that an Indiana man died of Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, were overdone.
"There is no mad cow disease," a floor source said.
Traders had speculated the man's death would cause a consumer panic and turn buyers away from beef, leading to weakening demand for livestock feeds.
Soymeal gained on news the FDA proposed tightening restrictions on the use of rendered carcasses in livestock feed. Soymeal would be a likely alternative if FDA tightened restrictions, traders said.
On the day, ADM sold 600 lots May soymeal and 100 lots December, FCC and Produce Grain each sold 200 July while Cargill Inc bought 350 May, 200 July, 50 August and 100 December, pit sources said.
Merrill Lynch sold 400 May soymeal and Rosenthal Collins bought 500 May.
In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought 300 lots May and 100 July while Produce Grain sold 300 lots each July and August and 200 September.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 18,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 21,451 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 15,000 lots, against Wednesday's 18,360.
